recipes.name: Greek lemon & feta
method: Heat oven to 200°C fan / 220°C conventional. Cut chicken into even 3 cm pieces; prepare vegetables as listed.
Use half of every ingredient per tray. Keep finishing ingredients aside. Spread shallowly; if crowded, add a tray or cook in batches.
Mix chicken, vegetables and flavour ingredients. Roast for 20 minutes, stir and swap shelves. Add feta and roast for another 10–15 minutes.
Check large pieces in both trays: 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds. Times are a guide; cook longer if needed.
Serve with: rice, wraps or separately roasted potatoes.

recipes.name: Fajita salsa & cheddar

ingredients.name: Fajita seasoning (60–80 g, check pack strength)

method: Heat oven to 200°C fan / 220°C conventional. Cut chicken into even 3 cm pieces; prepare vegetables as listed.
Use half of every ingredient per tray. Keep finishing ingredients aside. Spread shallowly; if crowded, add a tray or cook in batches.
Mix chicken, peppers, onions, seasoning and salsa. Roast for 20 minutes, stir and swap shelves. Scatter over cheddar and cook for another 10–15 minutes.
Check large pieces in both trays: 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds. Times are a guide; cook longer if needed.
Serve with: rice or wraps, with plain yoghurt at the table.

recipes.name: Harissa & chickpea

Use half of every ingredient per tray. Keep finishing ingredients aside. Spread shallowly; if crowded, add a tray or cook in batches.
Mix chicken, vegetables, chickpeas, tomatoes, harissa and cumin. Roast for 20 minutes, stir and swap shelves, then cook for another 15–20 minutes. Finish with lemon juice.
Check large pieces in both trays: 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds. Times are a guide; cook longer if needed.

recipes.name: Teriyaki & ginger
method: Heat oven to 200°C fan / 220°C conventional. Cut chicken into even 3 cm pieces; prepare vegetables as listed.
Use half of every ingredient per tray. Keep finishing ingredients aside. Spread shallowly; if crowded, add a tray or cook in batches.

Mix chicken, peppers, carrots, garlic, ginger and half the sauce. Roast for 15 minutes. Stir in broccoli and remaining sauce, swap shelves and roast for another 15–20 minutes. Add a splash of water if the glaze catches.
Check large pieces in both trays: 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds. Times are a guide; cook longer if needed.
Serve with: basmati rice or separately cooked noodles.

recipes.name: Tikka yoghurt chicken
method: Heat oven to 200°C fan / 220°C conventional. Cut chicken into even 3 cm pieces; prepare vegetables as listed.
Use half of every ingredient per tray. Keep finishing ingredients aside. Spread shallowly; if crowded, add a tray or cook in batches.

Mix yoghurt, tikka paste and lemon juice, then coat chicken and vegetables. Spread out and roast for 20 minutes. Stir, swap shelves and roast for another 10–15 minutes. The yoghurt may separate slightly as it cooks.
Check large pieces in both trays: 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds. Times are a guide; cook longer if needed.
Serve with: rice or warm flatbreads.
recipes.notes: Uses tikka *paste*, not a simmer sauce — they differ a lot in calories.

recipes.name: BBQ chicken & beans
method: Heat oven to 200°C fan / 220°C conventional. Cut chicken into even 3 cm pieces; prepare vegetables as listed.
Use half of every ingredient per tray. Keep finishing ingredients aside. Spread shallowly; if crowded, add a tray or cook in batches.
Mix chicken, vegetables, beans, sauce, paprika and 100 ml water. Roast for 20 minutes, stir and swap shelves. Add cheddar and roast for another 10–15 minutes. Loosen with a little water if needed.
Check large pieces in both trays: 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds. Times are a guide; cook longer if needed.
Serve with: rice.

recipes.name: Honey mustard chicken
method: Heat oven to 200°C fan / 220°C conventional. Cut chicken into even 3 cm pieces; prepare vegetables as listed.
Use half of every ingredient per tray. Keep finishing ingredients aside. Spread shallowly; if crowded, add a tray or cook in batches.

Mix the glaze ingredients. Toss chicken, carrots and onion with the glaze and roast for 15 minutes. Stir in broccoli, swap shelves and roast for another 15–20 minutes. Add a splash of water if the honey darkens too quickly.
Check large pieces in both trays: 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds. Times are a guide; cook longer if needed.
Serve with: rice or mashed potatoes; spoon over the cooking juices.

recipes.name: Shawarma-style chicken

Use half of every ingredient per tray. Keep finishing ingredients aside. Spread shallowly; if crowded, add a tray or cook in batches.
Mix oil, lemon, garlic and spices, then coat chicken and vegetables thoroughly. Roast for 20 minutes, stir and swap shelves, then cook for another 10–15 minutes. Spread well for more roasted edges.

recipes.name: Balsamic tomato & basil

Use half of every ingredient per tray. Keep finishing ingredients aside. Spread shallowly; if crowded, add a tray or cook in batches.
Mix chicken, vegetables, vinegar, oil, garlic and oregano. Roast for 20 minutes, stir and swap shelves, then cook for another 10–15 minutes. Stir in basil after cooking.
Check large pieces in both trays: 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds. Times are a guide; cook longer if needed.

recipes.name: Coconut curry chicken
method: Heat oven to 200°C fan / 220°C conventional. Cut chicken into even 3 cm pieces; prepare vegetables as listed.
Use half of every ingredient per tray. Keep finishing ingredients aside. Spread shallowly; if crowded, add a tray or cook in batches.

Mix chicken, peppers, cauliflower and sauce ingredients in deep-sided trays. Roast for 20 minutes, stir and swap shelves, then roast for another 15–20 minutes. Stir in spinach and cook for 3–5 minutes to wilt. Add lime juice.
Check large pieces in both trays: 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds. Times are a guide; cook longer if needed.
Serve with: basmati rice. Check curry paste ingredients for nuts.
recipes.notes: Curry pastes vary a lot (roughly 150–400 kcal per 100 g) — replace the generic figure with your jar’s label.

recipes.name: Cajun chicken & beans
method: Heat oven to 200°C fan / 220°C conventional. Cut chicken into even 3 cm pieces; prepare vegetables as listed.
Use half of every ingredient per tray. Keep finishing ingredients aside. Spread shallowly; if crowded, add a tray or cook in batches.

Mix all ingredients with 100 ml water and divide evenly between trays. Roast for 20 minutes, stir thoroughly and swap shelves, then cook for another 15–20 minutes. Add a little water if the sauce gets too thick.
Check large pieces in both trays: 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds. Times are a guide; cook longer if needed.
Serve with: rice or jacket potatoes. Seasoning blends may already contain salt.

recipes.name: Garlic mushroom & cream cheese
method: Heat oven to 200°C fan / 220°C conventional. Cut chicken into even 3 cm pieces; prepare vegetables as listed.
Use half of every ingredient per tray. Keep finishing ingredients aside. Spread shallowly; if crowded, add a tray or cook in batches.

Coat chicken and vegetables in oil, garlic and thyme. Roast for 20 minutes, stir and swap shelves, then cook for another 10–15 minutes. Loosen cream cheese with 100 ml hot water, stir into trays with spinach and return for 5 minutes until hot throughout.
Check large pieces in both trays: 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds. Times are a guide; cook longer if needed.
Serve with: pasta or rice. Stir well after reheating to bring the sauce back together.

Check large pieces in both trays: 75°C in the centre for 30 seconds. Times are a guide; cook longer if needed.
Serve with: rice or separately cooked noodles.

recipes.name: Basmati rice (by dry weight)
recipes.notes: Log the DRY weight. Nutrition is per dry gram — never log cooked grams against this.

recipes.name: Basmati rice (cooked batch)
method: Cook separately following the packet; no oil or butter.
Weigh all the cooked rice (without the container) and enter it on the batch.
recipes.notes: Log by cooked grams from the batch — its measured cooked weight turns them into dry-rice nutrition. 350 g dry = 7 small portions; use 700 g for 7 large.
